bands.name: Advanced readiness
bands.text: The foundations are strong. Validate the remaining gaps before entering a formal project gate.

bands.name: Prepared with gaps
bands.text: The organization has a workable base, but targeted actions should precede design and configuration.

bands.name: Developing readiness
bands.text: Several foundations are emerging. Close the lowest-scoring domains before committing to delivery dates.

bands.name: Foundation needed
bands.text: Core prerequisites are not yet consistent. Begin with governance, ownership, and a focused readiness plan.

domains.name: Governance and sponsorship
domains.description: Decision rights, scope, ownership, and executive support.
domains.recommendation: Confirm an accountable sponsor, decision rights, scope, and measurable outcomes before solution design.
questions: An accountable executive sponsor is identified and available for decisions.
The program scope, business outcomes, and success measures are documented.
Project roles, decision rights, and escalation paths are understood.

domains.name: Process ownership
domains.description: Current-state knowledge and ownership of future-state decisions.
domains.recommendation: Document priority processes and assign owners who can approve future-state decisions.
questions: Core business processes are documented at a level suitable for solution design.
Process owners can approve changes to the way work will be performed.
Known pain points and regulatory requirements are linked to target processes.

domains.name: Data readiness
domains.description: Data ownership, quality, migration scope, and validation.
domains.recommendation: Inventory source data, assign owners, and define quality and validation rules before migration planning.
questions: Source systems and data owners have been identified.
Material data-quality issues are known and have assigned remediation actions.
Migration validation rules and business sign-off responsibilities are defined.

domains.name: Testing and controls
domains.description: Acceptance criteria, end-to-end scenarios, and compliance evidence.
domains.recommendation: Define acceptance criteria and end-to-end scenarios early, including evidence for regulated controls.
questions: Business acceptance criteria are defined before configuration begins.
End-to-end test scenarios include critical operations and regulatory controls.
A formal method exists to record defects, decisions, approvals, and evidence.

domains.name: People and change readiness
domains.description: User participation, training, communications, and support transition.
domains.recommendation: Reserve user capacity for design and testing, then assign training, communication, and cutover support owners.
questions: Representative users are available for design reviews and acceptance testing.
Training and communication responsibilities are assigned to named owners.
The organization has a plan for cutover support and post-launch stabilization.
